Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the deposit share, the days before the event for the final payment, the days after the due date before a payment counts as late and the cost of money.
Check Clients and Billing Contacts: the terms in days, the payer note, the billing e-mail and the purchase order number. Missing details are flagged.
Check Contracts and Events, then enter every payment on Payment Schedule: deposit, instalments, final payment and extras. Days late, days to due and the open amount fill in.
Keep Invoices and Payments Received up to date. A payment that arrives is entered once; the month, the days after the due date and the client fill in.
Use Overdue Chase Log for every reminder and call. The promise check shows broken and pending promises, and Reminder Rules shows the next step for each kind of client.
Read Aged Receivables and Late Payer Watch every week to see who owes what and who to call first.
Enter extras on Extras and Change Orders and credits on Credits and Refunds. The amounts still to bill show in red until you fill the billed date.
Record due date moves on Payment Plan Changes and keep the Standard Payment Plans and Cancellation Scale for the offers you make to clients.
Event Cash Position and Proposal to Invoice Check show whether client money funds the vendor payments and whether anything agreed is not yet invoiced.
Monthly Invoicing and Weekly Cash from Clients give the collection rate, the overdue limit and the payments expected in the next 13 weeks.

Use the 14 calculators before you agree a plan: schedule, deposit, late payment cost, cash before the event, cancellation, extras, guest count, reminders, refund, stretch, slow payers, priority, funding, what-if.
Read Payments Dashboard and Charts every week: invoiced, received, overdue, extras, credits and the cash expected.
Know what an event will cost and earn before the day
Event budgets by guest count, quotes, reserve and margin for event planners
Budget by guest count and tier
type the guests and the budget per guest and every category gets its amount from your own category shares, with the planning fee and the contract value
every event and category shows budget, planned, agreed and actual cost with the variance, the cost per guest and an over plan flag
Event margin and cost per guest
planned and actual margin, margin share, cost per guest and the fee per labour hour for every event, with a flag for events below your target margin
every quote for a category side by side with the highest, the lowest, the rank and the saving of the quote you chose
Guest count change and lock date
the change from signing to now, its cost for the price per guest, the lock date and whether the count locked on time
what each use of the reserve paid for, the share used, the reserve left after each use and a warning before it is used up
every change after signing with the reason, the client approval and the owner approval flag, and every saved version of the budget with its change
fixed and variable cost by guest count band show the cost per guest and the saving against the smallest band, so you quote right at 60, 114 or 250 guests
Venue pricing with the minimum spend rule
hire fee, minimum spend, extra hours and the cost per guest for 100 guests, with the shortfall when the food and drink spend does not reach the minimum
Vendor price list with a validity check
the price of every vendor service for a 100-guest event, with prices that expire soon or have already expired
the planning fee divided by the hours the team really worked, per event and per event type, against the yield you want
spent, committed and still to book give the expected final cost, the overrun, the reserve left and the margin while there is time to act

Budget lines by event and category
One row per event and budget category with the budget, planned, agreed and actual cost; the cost to date, the variance to plan, the cost per guest and the over budget flag fill in by themselves.
Events with margin, cost per guest and plan check
One row per event with contract value and costs; the margin, cost per guest, plan check, hours logged, the fee per hour and what is not yet booked fill in by themselves.
Share of the budget by event type and category
The usual share of the client budget, the markup and the cost per guest for each category by event type, taken from past events; the amount for 100 guests fills in.
Cost per guest by event type and tier
The low, typical and high cost per guest for each event type and tier, from completed events; the range width and the typical cost for 100 guests fill in.
Fixed and variable cost by guest count band
Each guest count band with its fixed cost and its cost per guest; the cost per guest at the middle of the band and the saving against the smallest band fill in.
Catering menus with price per guest and bar
The menus you offer with the price per guest, the bar per guest and the minimum guests; the total for 100 guests (or the minimum, if higher) fills in.
The twelve venues with hire fee, minimum spend, set-up hours and curfew; the cost for 100 guests under the minimum spend rule and the cost per guest fill in.
Minimum spend not reached at 100 guests
Vendor price list with the price for 100 guests
One row per vendor service with the unit price, the minimum charge and how long the price is valid; the price for a 100-guest event and the validity check fill in.
Vendor quotes compared by event and category
One row per quote received for an event and category, with the one chosen; the highest and best quote, the saving of the chosen quote and the rank fill in.
One row per change of a category budget after signing, with the reason and whether the client approved; the new budget and the owner approval flag fill in.
One row per use of the reserve with what it paid for; the share of the reserve used, the reserve left after each use and the state of the reserve fill in.
Guest count at signing against now
One row per event with the guests at signing, the guests now and the day the count locked; the change, the cost impact, the lock date and the lock check fill in.
Planning fee share and hours by event type and tier
The fee share, the smallest fee and the hours allowed for each event type and tier; the fee on a 30,000 budget and the fee per hour fill in.
Markup and margin by budget category
The markup you add on vendor cost in each category and a typical vendor cost; the price and the margin on a 10,000 vendor cost fill in.
Hours allowed by event type and tier
The base hours and the hours per guest you allow for each event type and tier; the hours for 100 guests and the labour cost fill in.
Team hours and labour cost by event
One row per block of hours a team member worked on an event with the hourly cost; the labour cost fills in and feeds the fee per hour of each event.
Venue and vendor price index by month
One row per month with how much dearer or cheaper venues and vendors are and the demand level; the events that month and the price of a 10,000 base fill in.
Extras you sell with cost, price and margin
The extras clients ask for with your cost and your price; the margin share fills in so no extra is sold below the margin you want.
Tasting and sample costs against what the client pays
One row per tasting or sample with its cost and the amount billed to the client; the unbilled cost and the billing check fill in.
Budget versions with the change from the last one
One row per saved version of an event budget with the date, the total and the reason; the change from the previous version fills in.
